## Download

Download **`Rastro-windows-x64.exe`** below and run it. There's nothing to install. Windows will probably warn you the first time because the file isn't signed yet: click **More info → Run anyway**. The [README](https://github.com/MaxSala/rastro-tarkov#is-it-safe) explains why, and how to check the file yourself.

Already using Rastro? Close it and replace the old `.exe` with this one. Your settings, points, maps, prices and quest progress are kept.

## What's new

**Your quests follow the game**
- With raid detection on, the quests you accept, hand in or fail are ticked off by themselves, read from the game logs, separately for PvP and PvE.
- The first time, Rastro reads every launch the game has kept, so your progress catches up on its own. Accepting a quest also marks everything it requires as done and sets your level to fit.
- No logs left? **Catch up**: pick the last quest you completed for each trader, and everything before it is done.

**Plan the raid, then play it**
- **Raid plan** in the Quests panel (`5`): tick what you're doing this raid. The map shows only that, numbered along the shortest route, and Rastro tells you what to bring: markers, items to plant, keys.
- **Next** shows the next objective in big, with its distance and a button to be guided there.
- **To hand in** lists the quests that are ready, and which trader to see.

**Honest spots on the map**
- A badge is a precise place. An area shows its real outline. Small dots are the places an item **can** spawn: it's in one of them, not all of them.
- Every quest has its own colour when several share the map, and floors are now worked out from the bottom of each zone.
- See a spot that's wrong? **Wrong spot?** opens a GitHub issue with that objective's data, nothing about you.

**A section that looks like the game**
- Quests by trader, like the trader screen. **Now** shows what you're on and what you can start; **Items** lists what to keep for your quests, found in raid first.
- Your Kappa and Lightkeeper progress, and the map where you can get the most done.

**Fixes**
- The newest game log session is found by date, so a morning session is no longer mistaken for an older one.

Thanks to Casey Weed's [tarkov-map-companion](https://github.com/Battleroid/tarkov-map-companion) (MIT), whose work on the game logs showed how quest messages are written.

Full history in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/MaxSala/rastro-tarkov/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
